title: tcspecial physics model
description: The vehicle's physical elements, which tcssim's stand-ins measure and act on: a file of its own, named by each simulator file that uses it, because a vehicle's physics outlives any one configuration of its payloads. A simulated payload attaches to an element by its name and one of its terminals -- a sensor to an output, a heater to an input -- in the simulator file. YAML only.

physics.description: The elements, each of a type.

type.description: What kind of element it is, which decides what else it states. One kind so far: a thermal mass.

environment.description: The temperature around it, in kelvin. A mass starts here, with its heaters off, because a vehicle coming up cold is the case a thermostat exists for.

time_constant.description: How fast it loses the difference between itself and its environment, as a length of time: after one of these it has lost all but 1/e of it.

inputs.description: The names of the places a heater can be connected to it, separated by commas: `in1,in2`. None need be connected.

outputs.description: The names of the places a sensor can read its temperature from, separated by commas: `out1,out2,out3`. None need be connected. A name may be followed by `=` and how far, in kelvin, that place sits from the mass's temperature: `out2=+0.3`.

swing.description: How far the environment swings either side of `environment`, in kelvin, as a sine wave: a day and a night, or an orbit's sun and shadow.

period.description: How long one swing takes, as a length of time. Required with `swing` and refused without it.

wander.description: How far the environment wanders at random: the standard deviation, in kelvin, of a departure drawn back towards nought with `wander_time` as its time constant.

wander_time.description: How slowly the environment wanders, as a length of time. Required with `wander` and refused without it.

items.description: A thermal mass: one body at one temperature, which cools towards its environment and is warmed by the heaters that are on, so that what the vehicle reads is a consequence of what the vehicle drove. Three sensors reading one mass agree, where three sending random bytes never do. A mass nothing is attached to is refused.
